correctness.rationale: The derivative-measure coupling rigorously reduces the real periodic \(BV\) norm to a pair of jumps; locality for \(N\ge6\) avoids complementary interactions. Exact single-step residuals give \(J\le1/6\). Direct integration yields \(Q=d-7d^2/12-(d-1/4)(a-b)^2\) and unique maximum at \(d=6/7\), \(a=b=3/7\). Other separations are excluded by explicit overlap formulas and rational Bernstein positivity: minimum coefficients \(1/672\), \(47/1792\), and \(1/1344\). Equality rays imply one arc up to constants and scaling. The standalone rational checker reproduces certificates and 3,379 supplementary pulse comparisons; finite samples are not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: The original box-averaged hat quasi-interpolant appears in the 2012 open manuscript arXiv:1211.1069v1, whose Theorem 3.9 gives nonspecific \(L^1\) and general \(L^p\) bounds, not the exact one-dimensional periodic \(BV\)-to-\(L^2\) squared norm \(3/(28N)\) or two-jump rigidity. The known real-line \(L^1\)/\(L^\infty\) hat-error frontier in accessible prior claim 82353e3e has a different codomain and does not determine the pair cross term. Orthogonal-spline least-squares projectors use a distinct reconstruction. Nagler and coauthors study point-sampled Schoenberg operators and spectral/modulus estimates. No covering implication was found; unindexed equivalence and inaccessible 2015 journal refinements remain risks.

value.rationale: This is the sharp error of a canonical positive total-variation-diminishing finite-element quasi-interpolant used for discontinuous data. It gives a non-implied exact \(BV\)-to-\(L^2\) norm across every uniform periodic grid with \(N\ge6\), classifies every extremizer, and identifies a genuinely two-jump interaction at phases \(1/14\) and \(13/14\), inaccessible to isolated-step optimization or generic \(L^p\) estimates. The threshold \(N\ge6\) is justified by noninteraction of boundary layers and is not claimed optimal.
